claim.pdf_says: Heading '14.6.13.1.3   Fatal exception conditions' - a fifth-level clause number, the sibling of 14.6.13.1.1 and 14.6.13.1.2.
claim.why_it_matters: Same defect as 14.6.13.1.2: at '##' it is two levels shallower than sibling 14.6.13.1.1 ('####') and shallower than its parent 14.6.13.1 ('###'). This clause is cross-referenced by 14.6.3 on page 569 and by 14.6.13.1.4, so its outline placement matters for navigation.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. I rendered specs page 579 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v579/spec_p579.png) and read the printed glyphs directly. The PDF prints exactly one heading on this page, in bold serif: '14.6.13.1.3 Fatal exception conditions'. specs/ISO_COBOL.md carries that heading verbatim - same clause number, same title, same spelling and capitalization - preceded by its navigation anchor: 24205: 24206: ## 14.6.13.1.3 Fatal exception conditions The claim is filed as kind='missing-heading', but the heading is present. The claim's own narrative concedes this by quoting the markdown line that contains it. No text is absent, reflowed away, or lost. Every one of the page's eight numbered rules, both NOTEs, and the running head are likewise present and faithful. (2) THE DIFFERENCE IS PURE MARKDOWN FORMATTING, NOT CONTENT. The only asserted difference is the count of '#' characters. A print PDF encodes no markdown heading depth - there is no '####' in the source document to lose. Outline position in ISO/IEC 1989:2023 is carried by the dotted decimal clause number itself ('14.6.13.1.3'), and that number is transcribed exactly. This falls squarely under the reject criterion 'the difference is only ... formatting' and 'the difference does not change meaning'. (3) THE STATED NAVIGATION HARM DOES NOT OCCUR. Cross-references from 14.6.3 and from 14.6.13.1.4 resolve by clause number and by the '#section-14-6-13-1-3' anchor, both of which are present and correct. The '#' count participates in neither. No link, anchor, or reference is broken by the depth. (4) THE CLAIM'S FACTUAL PREMISE IS WRONG. It asserts '####' is the sibling norm. Actual depths in specs/ISO_COBOL.md for the 14.6.13.1.x family: 24148: #### 14.6.13.1.1 General 24190: ## 14.6.13.1.2 Normal completion of a declarative procedure 24206: ## 14.6.13.1.3 Fatal exception conditions 24240: ### 14.6.13.1.4 Nonfatal exception conditions 24253: ### 14.6.13.1.5 Exception objects 24289: ### 14.6.13.1.6 Exception-names and exception conditions The '####' of .1 is a minority of one; the plurality of siblings is '###'. There is no established convention here for .3 to violate. The arbitrariness is proven outright by a duplicated transcription block in the same region: 14.6.13.1.1 appears at line 24107 as '## 14.6.13.1.1 General' and again at line 24148 as '#### 14.6.13.1.1 General' - the identical heading emitted at two different depths. Depth assignment in this transcription is non-semantic noise, so a depth mismatch is not evidence of a PDF-to-markdown content discrepancy. Secondary misquote: the claim cites 'Line 24203'. The heading is at line 24206; 24203 is blank-adjacent body text ('2) Any directly or indirectly activated runtime element terminates the run unit.' region). The claim misquotes the markdown location by three lines. One genuine (and different) transcription defect was observed incidentally and is NOT what was claimed: lines ~24086-24124 duplicate lines ~24127-24165 (the whole 14.6.12 / 14.6.13 / 14.6.13.1 / 14.6.13.1.1 run appears twice, with differing heading depths). That is a duplicated-block issue on the pages preceding 579 and should be filed separately if not already tracked. It does not make the page-579 claim real.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. The heading '14.6.13.1.3   Fatal exception conditions' is printed on PDF page 579 and is transcribed verbatim at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 24206 (the claim says 24203), with its '#section-14-6-13-1-3' anchor intact. Nothing is missing, so 'missing-heading' is the wrong kind. The sole difference is the markdown '#' depth, which is presentational, absent from the PDF source, and irrelevant to cross-reference resolution - references use the dotted clause number and the anchor. The claim's premise that '####' is the sibling norm is false: of the six 14.6.13.1.x siblings only .1 uses '####', .2 and .3 use '##', and .4/.5/.6 use '###'; 14.6.13.1.1 itself is emitted at two different depths in a duplicated block (lines 24107 and 24148), showing depth here is non-semantic noise. Separately and unclaimed: lines ~24086-24124 are a verbatim duplicate of ~24127-24165, a real transcription defect on the pages before 579 that warrants its own ledger entry.
